Fixed: The visible verification page now opens the same catalogue URL that the app checks, instead of opening the homepage while checking a different page.
The visible page, manual app confirmation and opt-in cookie diagnosis share one catalogue target.
Changed: Complete any challenge on the catalogue page, wait until catalogue cards appear, then select Verify & return. No automatic completion or challenge solving is performed.
This tests the homepage-versus-catalogue mismatch. Site acceptance still needs confirmation on Windows; a successful homepage alone is insufficient.
The default-browser fallback and standalone updater are retained.

Added: Open in browser in the verification toolbar launches the configured site homepage in your default browser for direct, user-controlled browsing and watching.
Changed: The fallback sends no app cookies, credentials, history or playback data to the browser. Browser sessions and playback progress are separate; app verification is not marked successful.
The toolbar explains the separate browser session and handles Windows browser-launch failures.
Manual Verify & return, opt-in diagnosis and the standalone updater are retained. Native app catalogue verification remains unresolved.

Fixed: Removed the automatic catalogue check on the first verification page load, which could occur while the CAPTCHA was still displayed.
Changed: Verification now waits for you to complete the CAPTCHA and press Verify & return. That action flushes the latest cookies before checking actual app catalogue access.
Page loads alone neither read verification cookies nor trigger catalogue checks. Diagnose remains an explicit, confirmed action.
This fixes the premature check timing; successful access to the site still needs confirmation on Windows. The beta 7 standalone updater is retained.

Fixed: The standalone updater now requests main-app window closure directly, including when launched outside the app, rather than depending on the app’s status-file monitor.
The updater waits for path-matched main/player processes to exit, then checks exclusive access to existing application files before replacement. Persistent locks stop installation before copying.
Added: A force-close choice for unresponsive processes after normal closure is attempted. It is limited to this installation; the updater and other installation folders are excluded. Declining stops the install.
Numeric close-request, force-stop-request and remaining-process counts in exported updater diagnostics.
Changed: The separate updater still verifies downloads and prepares rollback files before requesting app closure. History and favorites stay in the Windows profile.
Existing verification diagnostics are retained. The site-verification issue remains unresolved.

Added: Opt-in Diagnose action in the verification window. A native privacy confirmation precedes a bounded metadata-only capture during one ordinary catalogue check.

Filtered Chromium cookie inclusion/exclusion counts, partition flags, network-delegate blocking count and fixed reason codes in exported diagnostics. Cookie values, names, URLs and raw traces are excluded from the exported summary.
Changed: Temporary metadata can contain URLs and network details. Sensitive capture modes are never enabled. Temporary traces are removed after analysis; cleanup failures are reported and stale app-owned traces are retried at startup.
This is an investigation build. The site-verification issue remains unresolved; requests, browser identity and access protections are unchanged. The standalone updater is retained.

Added: PopcornPalaceUpdater.exe: a separate Windows updater with download progress and its own Install and restart button. The runtime is bundled; users do not need to install .NET.
Direct updater launch support. Both app-launched and directly launched updates run from a temporary copy outside the installation folder, allowing both EXEs to be replaced.
Fixed: The main app stays open through download, checksum verification, extraction and rollback preparation. Only the updater’s confirmed install step requests app exit.
Native download verification, bounded ZIP extraction, file-lock retries and rollback replace the PowerShell installation helper.
Changed: The app’s update prompt now opens the separate updater window. Download and installation are performed by the second EXE. Saved history and favorites remain in the Windows profile.
The site-verification issue remains unresolved. Existing numeric verification diagnostics are retained.

Added: Diagnostic build for the unresolved Windows verification failure. Observes whether the browser and background requests send cookies, whether the clearance cookie is present, and the resulting HTTP status.

Cookie-store presence and metadata checks, same-origin redirect flags, and separate challenge-header/markup flags. Logs contain numeric flags and counts only; cookie values, URLs, titles, credentials and raw headers are never recorded.
Fixed: The verification toolbar now identifies the rejected application check and displays its HTTP status instead of repeatedly asking for an already completed site check.
Changed: Automatic access checking runs once per verification window; further checks require Return to app. Network requests, cookies and browser protections are not modified by the observers.
This is an investigation build, not a confirmed verification fix. Open Verify site, let the page load, select Return to app once, close the window and export diagnostics.

Fixed: Replaced whole-folder renaming with in-place application file replacement, with retries for files still locked by Windows.
The app stays open while the update helper checks the package, extracts it, tests write access and saves rollback files. It only exits after the helper reports ready.
Preparation errors remain visible in the app. Failed replacement attempts restore saved files and reopen the previous app when recovery succeeds.
Added: Numeric update installation stages, Windows error codes and rollback status in exported diagnostics.
A visible preparing-update state that prevents repeated install clicks.
Changed: Users on beta 1 or beta 2 whose installer closes without restarting should manually extract this ZIP into a new writable folder once. Saved history and favorites remain in the Windows profile.

Fixed: The site-verification window now has a persistent Return to app toolbar. It confirms catalogue access using the same session before returning and retrying the interrupted search, title or episode.
Closing or cancelling verification no longer reports successful verification. Failed checks stay visible in the window; completion never overrides a different screen opened later.
Ordinary pages containing a Cloudflare Turnstile widget are no longer automatically treated as blocked pages. Actual challenge response headers and interstitials are still respected.
Application requests retain the verified browser user agent and same-origin request context while keeping cookies restricted to their original origin.
Added: Verification-stage and parsed-catalogue-count events in the existing privacy-filtered local diagnostics.
Changed: The site remains in an isolated browser view with no application bridge or Node access. The Return to app toolbar is trusted local content. No challenge solving or protection bypass is automated.

Added: First Windows 10/11 x64 portable build, following the Android 0.6.24 app's catalogue, category, search and library behavior.
Discover, Movies, TV Shows, anime sub/dub movie/series sections, Audiobooks, genre filters and sorting. Search stays in the selected section; Discover searches all categories.
Title details, season selectors and numerically ordered episode lists, favorites with multiple custom categories, watched-only history/finished sections, and Continue Watching removal with Undo.
Video and audiobook playback, resume positions, approximate watch time, manual watched toggles, automatic watched marking near completion, and Next episode marking the episode being left as watched.
Keyboard and mouse controls, full screen, volume, seeking, minimized playback and system media controls where supported by Windows.
Android/Windows JSON backup import and export, visible site verification and session clearing, local diagnostic viewing/export/disable/clear, and offline changelog.
Independent Windows GitHub update checks on opening/foreground, size/SHA-256 verification, and confirmed installation/restart for portable installations.
Changed: Windows uses Chromium and hls.js rather than Android Media3. Codec and site compatibility require testing on a Windows PC.
Closing the window exits the app; minimizing it continues playback. Opening an in-app list pauses playback, matching Android.
Public repository contains release packages, update metadata and documentation. Development source and user data are kept private. No app source or session logs are published separately.
